items.title: I-adic completeness of a module is equivalent to the vanishing of its torsion functors and surjectivity onto its completion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma relates I-adic completeness of a module to the vanishing of the torsion functors T(M, f) for f in I, and states the converse as surjectivity of the completion map when I is finitely generated (statement lines 25962-25970). Both directions are explicit: for the first, the proof reduces to the vanishing of Hom and Ext from A_f and then splits an arbitrary extension by an infinite series that converges precisely because M is complete, while for the second it builds, from an arbitrary sequence x_n, the extension of M by A_f whose relations are x_n - f e_{n+1} + e_n = 0, splits it using the vanishing assumption and finishes with the snake lemma (proof lines 25973-26014). The construction of the infinite series in part (1) and the construction of the universal extension in part (2) are the two substantive steps. The counted span refers to one lemma of this chapter and one lemma of another chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
